extensions.scope: Design system v2 ("ds"), rolled out page by page. Migrated so far: /guests, /guests/list. Every other screen and the app shell keep the incumbent T styles and components/ui.tsx until they migrate. Guest-facing palettes G and P are out of scope.

surface.purpose: Cards, groups, tasks, tiles, fields, ghost buttons, chips.

ink-2.purpose: Secondary copy that reads as content.

track.purpose: Meter track and waiting segment, calm icon, skeleton.

accent.purpose: Fills and dots only; never text.

accent-strong.purpose: Filled button, links, selected chip, focus outline, rosewood text.

cant.purpose: Can't: fills only; text falls back to muted.

display.purpose: The page title, one per page; 44px from 960px.

numeral.purpose: The one figure a hub leads with; tabular.

lede.purpose: A statement replacing the numeral; empty-state titles.

body.purpose: Quiet paragraphs and task bodies, in muted.

caption.purpose: Row metadata, tile meta, tile group labels.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: ds-card only: the lead summary and empty states.

shadows.name: inset-outline
shadows.purpose: Ghost buttons, chips, fields, back button.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible on rows, tiles, links, buttons, chips, back, summary (-2px inside groups).

motion.name: state

motion.name: meter-fill
motion.purpose: Meter segments easing to their counts.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes meter, row, button, field, tile transitions and stops the shimmer.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Couple's Desk"**

A calm, warm working surface that belongs to Union and to nobody's wedding. Cream canvas, white-cream cards drawn with hairlines, warm ink, one modern grotesque, and a single rosewood voice for the action that matters. The palette is Union's incumbent colours (rosewood, cream, warm ink, sage, dusty blue, sand, amber), renamed by role and given the darker shades that make text pass WCAG AA.

Union is theme-neutral (PRODUCT.md, principle 5): the interface never takes on a wedding style, so it cannot exclude a bohemian, black-tie, minimal or rustic couple. Personality comes from the couple's own details (their names and date under the page title), never from the chrome. A themed "garden marquee" trial and a black-and-white neutral frame were both rejected; this is the middle path.

The density is phone-first and Operate-mode: short visits, one-tap actions, large type for the one number that matters, quiet type for everything else. On desktop the same content opens into two columns rather than growing new furniture.
keyCharacteristics: Union's own colours named by role; text only in the roles that pass AA.
One face (Hanken Grotesk) at a few tight sizes, weight 600 for anything that names something.
Flat hairline surfaces; only the summary card and the filled button lift.
One filled rosewood button per area; everything else is ghost or link.
Reply status always uses the same four-colour vocabulary: coming, maybe, can't, waiting.

rules.name: The AA Text Rule
rules.body: Text takes only `ink`, `ink-2`, `muted`, `accent-strong`, `coming-strong`, `maybe` or `waiting-strong`. `accent`, `coming`, `cant` and `waiting` are for fills, dots and rings, never for letters.

rules.name: The Rosewood Voice Rule
rules.body: Rosewood Deep marks what you can act on: the one filled button, links, the selected chip, the focused element. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The Waiting Ring Rule
rules.body: Not answering is an absence, so it is drawn hollow: an amber ring on the pending face and the legend dot, and plain track in the meter. Only the answers get solid colour.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Heading Rule
rules.body: Section headings are Headline type in sentence case. No uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow or kicker above or in place of a heading.

rules.name: The One Number Rule
rules.body: A hub leads with at most one Numeral; everything else is Title size or below.

rules.name: The Quiet Lift Rule
rules.body: Groups, rows, tasks and tiles are flat with a 1px hairline. Only the lead card and the filled button cast a shadow, so the eye goes to the summary and to the action.

dos: Do take every colour from `DS` / `--ds-*` by role; hex lives only in `lib/theme.ts`.
Do set text in the AA roles only (see the contrast table); keep `accent`, `coming`, `cant` and `waiting` for shapes.
Do give each area one filled Rosewood Deep button; make the rest ghost buttons or links.
Do show reply status with the shared four-state vocabulary (face, status, dot, meter) and the `is-attending | is-maybe | is-declined | is-pending` modifiers.
Do put the couple's names and date under the page title; that is where personality lives.
Do use tabular figures for counts and skeletons shaped like the content while loading.
Do keep touch targets at 44px (40px for small buttons and the back button) and inputs at 16px text.
donts: Don't mix `T` styles or `components/ui.tsx` pieces with `ds-*` classes inside one page.
Don't add wedding motifs, themed ornaments or a per-wedding colour to the interface (PRODUCT.md principle 5).
Don't set uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrows or kickers above headings; headings are sentence case.
Don't put `waiting-strong` text on `track` (4.41:1) or any text in `accent`, `coming`, `cant` or `waiting`.
Don't add shadows to groups, rows, tasks or tiles; only the lead card and the filled button lift.
Don't show a placeholder zero while data loads.
